summary: Today, Grace Hill's point solutions (Training, Surveys, Policies, Mystery Shopping, Reputation Management, Intelligence+, Realync, HelloData®) are each priced and packaged on their own, with no shared PHQ commercial structure. Result: no ready-to-go package puts related solutions together, ~79% of GH-Success and ~50% of Mid-Market/Enterprise customers buy only one product, and there's no clear expansion path. The new structure organizes around the two workflows buyers actually own — Workforce Excellence (L&D/Ops) and Resident & Prospect Experience (Marketing) — with PHQ Platform Core as the included data & intelligence foundation across both, and a standardized per-unit commercial model. It is a three-decision purchase: (1) pick your workflow track(s), (2) pick your data & intelligence tier — PHQ Platform Core (foundation, included) or PHQ Platform Plus (+$0.59/unit/month upgrade), (3) add add-ons as needed. The October deck's one-line version: know what matters, act on it, see what changed — because NOI pressure never stops, and seeing where performance falls short is not the same as knowing how to improve it.

discountFramework.recommended: Same step-downs across every package: 1,000–3,999 = list; 4,000–9,999 = -10%; 10,000–19,999 = -17.5%; 20,000+ = -17.5%. Today the buckets and rates vary by point solution (lowest: Training, highest: Policies) — this standardizes them.

Proposed in the Sept 16 working session as a new 10% discount for 3+ year terms, standard annual price increases still apply. CONTESTED IN THE ROOM (Sept 16): Sales leadership (Ashlee Horn) pushed back hard on making a multi-year discount standard — 56% of this quarter's contracts sold multi-year with no discount offered, and giving away margin by default risks eating into deal size given packages are already bundled/discounted. RML (Navi) agreed to take it offline and revisit an alternative: 3-year term as the standard list price, with a modest premium for a more flexible 1- or 2-year term, rather than a discount for going long. Neither the Sept 30 nor the October messaging deck resolves this — they cover naming, packaging and the pilot plan, not discount mechanics. Do not present the 10%-for-3-years figure as settled until this is resolved.

corePitch.source: October 2026 messaging deck, slide 2 — “the Grace Hill pitch, on one page.” Replaces the Sept 30 version's “Prove it worked” framing with “See what changed.”
corePitch.theProblem: NOI pressure never stops. Seeing where performance falls short is not the same as knowing how to improve it. Operators have plenty of data. The harder part is knowing what matters, what to do next and what changed.
corePitch.forWhom: Multifamily owners and operators. Mid-market and enterprise.
corePitch.whyGraceHill: Grace Hill connects experience, performance and the market. PerformanceHQ brings together feedback, team and property performance, 30+ years of benchmarks and market context, then connects findings to action.
corePitch.whyNow: Teams are being asked to improve more with fewer resources. Another report is not enough.
corePitch.whatGraceHillDoes: Know what matters. Act on it. See what changed. Surface the priority. Recommend the next step. Get action to the right person. See how performance moves.

corePitch.whyGraceHillCanDoIt: It sees what others see in pieces: resident and employee feedback, mystery shops, property performance, 30+ years of benchmarks, and HelloData market and competitive context — connected under PerformanceHQ, instead of scattered across separate tools (training completion, survey scores, review ratings, leasing results, operational data, market comps, spreadsheets) that each show only part of the picture.

problemFirstMessaging.howToUse: Outside-in, VBF order (Value → Benefit → Feature) per Grace Hill's messaging framework: open with the problem/outcome the buyer already cares about, then the benefit, then how Grace Hill delivers it — the package and its features come last, as the mechanism, not the headline. corePitch above is the master four-line version of this; the per-track detail below is the expanded version for each buyer.

tracks.problem: Your team's execution is inconsistent from property to property, compliance risk sits on whoever happens to be on shift, and you can't tell whether that's a training gap, a policy gap, or a people problem until something has already gone wrong.
tracks.outcome: Build the team behind a consistent experience — every employee, at every property, working to the same standard, with the gap caught and closed before residents feel it.
tracks.benefit: You get ahead of the audit or the incident instead of reacting to it, and you can prove — not just hope — that your team is trained, policy-acknowledged, and performing to standard.
tracks.howWeDeliverIt: Training, policies, and mystery shopping working together under PerformanceHQ — industry-specific courseware, policy acknowledgment tracking, and on-site performance verification — packaged as Compliance, Core, or Plus depending on how far past baseline compliance you need to go.
tracks.proof: 64% of positive resident reviews mention the onsite team; one new hire costs about $4,700; 500,000+ multifamily professionals trained at 2,800+ companies.

tracks.problem: You don't have a reliable read on how residents and prospects actually feel about your properties until they leave a bad review, don't renew, or don't tour — and by then it's too late to do anything but react.
tracks.outcome: Improve the experience from tour through renewal — catching sentiment and leasing friction early enough to act on it, instead of finding out from a lost renewal or a 2-star review.
tracks.benefit: Fewer surprises at renewal, a reputation that supports (instead of undercuts) your marketing spend, and a leasing experience that converts more of the tours you're already paying for.
tracks.howWeDeliverIt: Resident and prospect surveys, reputation management, and Realync's leasing video tools working off the same PerformanceHQ data layer — packaged as Sentiment Core, Leasing Core, or Plus depending on whether the bigger gap is sentiment, conversion, or both.
tracks.proof: 41% of negative reviews during unit turnover are about maintenance; a turn costs about $3,872; up to 20% higher renewal intent than the national average with more than one Grace Hill tool.

sharedLayer.problem: You're making decisions about your portfolio without knowing how you stack up against the market — rents, comps, competitive positioning — which means every pricing and positioning call is a guess.
sharedLayer.outcome: Confidence that your people-performance and property-performance decisions are grounded in real market data, not internal signals alone.
sharedLayer.howWeDeliverIt: HelloData®, included as HelloData® Lite in every PHQ Platform Core package and available at full depth (HelloData® Complete) in PHQ Platform Plus — or standalone for teams (e.g., acquisitions, investment) that only need market data, not the workflow tracks.

objectionHandling.a: Buying starts with the business need, not a product list: fewer decisions, and a clear path to add more later.

Grace Hill connects what residents and employees experience with how teams and properties perform, 30+ years of benchmarks, and market and competitive context. Then it connects those findings to actions through training, policies, coaching and PerformanceHQ action plans.

objectionHandling.q: Why should I choose Grace Hill instead of a competitor?
objectionHandling.a: Grace Hill brings together a breadth of multifamily capabilities that's hard to replicate with a single alternative. You solve more needs within one ecosystem, and the value multiplies as those capabilities work together through PerformanceHQ rather than across disconnected systems.

objectionHandling.q: I only need Training / Surveys / Realync. Why do I need to move to a broader package?
objectionHandling.a: You don't need to buy the entire Grace Hill ecosystem. Start with the narrowest standard package that solves the need you have today, then expand only when another use case becomes relevant. The packages themselves stay intact — this preserves focused entry points without recreating à-la-carte complexity.

objectionHandling.q: Do all of my properties have to be on the same package?
objectionHandling.a: No. We can match the package to the parts of your portfolio where it makes sense, rather than forcing every property into the same configuration. GH Success and lower Mid-Market stay on one standard configuration; for eligible larger portfolios, Guided Flexibility can apply different standard packages across defined property groups; true property-level customization is Bespoke/CPQ, reserved for strategic accounts.

objectionHandling.q: What if I need more mystery shops, or want to allocate them differently across my portfolio?
objectionHandling.a: You have flexibility beyond what's included in the package. Core includes two shops a year and Plus includes four, but you can change the shop type or increase the frequency based on your needs, and you can always purchase additional shops on demand, above what's in the package.

objectionHandling.q: I only want a one-year contract. Why do I have to commit to multiple years?
objectionHandling.a: You don't have to — one-year contracts remain available. NOTE: the exact multi-year incentive structure (discount-for-3-years vs. premium-for-flexibility) was still being resolved as of Sept 16 — see discountFramework.
